input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The condition `all(arg.help is not None ...)` contradicts the docstring ("if at least one is documented") and should be `any`. With `all`, a command with a mix of documented and undocumented arguments shows no arguments section. A command with no arguments passes `all([])` and gets an empty "Positional arguments" section.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with two arguments where only one has help. `all` returns False, so the section is skipped and the documented argument's help disappears from the output. Trigger 2: a command with zero arguments. `all` on an empty list returns True, so the code writes a section header with an empty list.
critique: The finding identifies the same all-vs-any guard error. It also gives both failure paths: with mixed documentation the section is skipped, and with zero arguments all([]) is True, so an empty header is printed.
